headline: President Trump is expected to name intelligence chief Jay Clayton as the White House's AI czar, a job he would hold alongside his current one, according to news reports.
score_reason: Pool score kept: widely reported by several outlets and an AI lead in the White House matters, but nothing is announced yet.
importance_line: If it happens, one official would hold the AI czar role while also overseeing the spy agencies, which affects AI companies, Congress and the public; Trump has so far favoured AI companies policing themselves, and nothing is official yet.
summary: CNN reports, citing two unnamed sources, that President Trump is expected to pick Jay Clayton, the director of national intelligence, as AI czar and could announce it as early as Friday 2 October, with Clayton keeping his intelligence job. New since Axios reported on 30 Sep 2026 that Trump had only floated Clayton: CNN and NBC News now report he is the expected pick, though a White House official called such reporting "baseless speculation" until the President announces it.
notes: Original outlet Reuters (relaying CNN; blocked, 401). Written from CNN and NBC News. Continues the 30 Sep 2026 Axios story (C13-10 in the 1 Oct pool). New today: several outlets say he is the expected pick; still unannounced.
